title: Cross-lingual embedset randomized cluster checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working checklist and protocol for running a randomized cluster sanity+relevance probe across multilingual embedsets during model onboarding and regression runs. Target audience: applied-ml engineers and solutions reviewers who need a quick, reproducible set of checks that surface obvious regressions (semantic collapse, language-dropping, cluster fragmentation) before longer manual evals.

High-level approach (why randomized):
- Instead of hand-curating only positive examples, pick stratified random anchors from the embedset by language and domain.
- For each anchor, fetch nearest neighbors (k=10) from the candidate index and compute automated signals (pairwise cosine, silhouette, language-consistency).
- Surface the top N suspicious anchors for human spot-checking (N=50 by default) to find failure modes that scripted metrics miss.

Minimum inputs (what you need before running):
- baseline_model_id: string (the currently accepted model, e.g., rwd-embed-v3-2026-01)
- candidate_model_id: string (new model under test)
- embedset_id: string (which dataset to test; supports mixed-language label)
- languages: list of languages to stratify by (e.g., ["en","es","fr","zh"])
- seed: integer for RNG reproducibility

Sampling and stratification procedure:
1) Determine per-language sample budget: default 1k per language or 10% of language shard, whichever is smaller.
2) Within a language shard, stratify by token-length quartile to catch short vs long context failures.
3) Randomly draw anchors with seed and record indices in output (anchor_ids.txt).
4) For each anchor, retrieve top-10 nearest neighbors from both baseline and candidate indexes.

Automated metrics to compute (per-anchor and aggregate):
- avg_cosine_diff: mean(candidate_cosine - baseline_cosine) across neighbors (string)
- top1_switch_rate: fraction of anchors where top-1 neighbor changed identity between models
- lang_consistency_rate: fraction of top-10 neighbors matching anchor language (detect language drop)
- silhouette_delta: silhouette(candidate_clusters) - silhouette(baseline_clusters) computed on anchor neighborhoods (catch fragmentation)
- redundancy_ratio: percent of neighbors that are near-duplicates (high = potential collapsed clusters)

Threshold heuristics (quick triage rules):
- avg_cosine_diff < -0.04 and top1_switch_rate > 0.25 -> immediate regression flag
- lang_consistency_rate drop > 0.2 for low-resource language -> escalate to multilingual owner
- silhouette_delta < -0.05 -> investigate embedding spread; likely quality regression
These are heuristics intended for triage; treat as signals, not hard blockers.

Human spot-check protocol (50 anchors):
- Prioritize anchors where multiple signals align (e.g., large negative avg_cosine_diff + lang inconsistency).
- For each flagged anchor: paste anchor text + top-10 baseline vs top-10 candidate (with cosines) into review doc. Annotator marks: Good/Acceptable/Bad and writes 1-line rationale.
- Collect 3 independent annotations for a random 20% subset to estimate annotator agreement.

Quick CLI examples (working commands used in embedset-tools repo):
- export SEED=42
- python probes/run_random_cluster_probe.py --embedset my-multilang-2025 --baseline rwd-embed-v3-2026-01 --candidate rwd-embed-v4-2026-02 --langs en,es,fr,zh --sample-per-lang 500 --out out/run-2026-02-28
- python probes/compute_aggregate_metrics.py --in out/run-2026-02-28 --metrics-path out/metrics.json
- scripts/spotcheck_to_doc.sh out/run-2026-02-28/flagged-anchors.csv > out/spotcheck-for-review.md

Artifacts produced (what to save to the run folder):
- anchors.csv (seeded sample with language, token_count, shard_id)
- neighbors_baseline.csv, neighbors_candidate.csv (top-k with cosine scores)
- metrics_summary.json (aggregate metrics and thresholds applied)
- flagged-anchors.csv (ordered by failure score)
- spotcheck_review.md (human annotation template + collected judgments)

Regression gating recommendation (ops):
- If regression flag triggers and more than 10% of sampled anchors are labeled Bad by human spot-checkers -> block rollout and run deeper evals.
- If signals are mixed, schedule 1-week extended eval on curated gold queries and request developer writeup.

Notes on multilingual gotchas we've seen (lessons learned):
- Subword tokenization differences lead to consistent length-bias across languages; include length stratification.
- Tiny-language shards can be noisy; use upsampling + caution on thresholds.
- Quantized model variants can show modest global cosine shifts; compute per-language baselines and de-bias by mean-centering cosines before comparing.
- Near-duplicate web noise (boilerplate) can inflate redundancy_ratio; add a cheap fuzzy-dedup step (MinHash) in preprocessing.

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Add automatic language detection confidence filter; many anchors have mixed-language content.
- Decide final gating thresholds per customer tier (enterprise customers may need stricter rules).
- Integrate with Redwood Console experiment traces so reviewers can click from flagged anchor -> request timeline.

Reviewer checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm seed and embedset id match release candidate run
- [ ] Verify per-language sample sizes look reasonable (no 0s)
- [ ] Inspect top 20 flagged anchors for obvious false positives (boilerplate, spam)
- [ ] Run 3 random manual checks in low-resource languages
- [ ] Attach spotcheck_review.md and metrics_summary.json to the ticket (JIRA attached above)

Appendix: suggested human annotation rubric (one-line):
- Good: candidate model neighbors are as (or more) relevant than baseline; language preserved
- Acceptable: some minor reorder but relevance preserved
- Bad: candidate neighbors are off-topic, wrong language, or show duplicate collapse

If you run this and want me to standardize outputs into a Confluence template, ping @aisha in slack and attach out/metrics.json with run metadata.
